## Intent
Hypothesis: compiler auto-vectorization of the integration loop, fused with a register-resident decide+respawn+render scatter, can approach the streaming ceiling across death rates.

## Layout & approach
The AoS layout at 68 B/p offers only 24 hot bytes (35%) to loop 1 and 36 (52%) to loop 2 — the rest is dead weight in every cache line. Fusing decide+respawn+render eliminates intermediate storage, keeping the death verdict in registers. Identity ordering gives sequential stride-68B access. Working set spills L1d at N≈963 and L2 at N≈61680, but because only 35–52% of each record is touched, the effective working set is roughly half the nominal size.

## Cache saturation
The ns/p curve is strikingly flat. At q=0.01 it ranges 6.15–6.89 ns/p from L1d (N=380) through DRAM (N=10M). The L1d→L2 transition at N≈963 produces no knee (6.60→6.75). The L2→DRAM transition at N≈61680 shows slight improvement (6.51→6.34) — DRAM prefetch amortizes sequential stride better than contended L2. The dense grid resolves both transitions but neither is a cliff; the low hot fraction and sequential access keep the memory subsystem fed regardless of cache level.

## Bandwidth
The memory floor is 2.274 ns/p; at q=0.01 the algo runs at 2.7–3.0× the floor — two-thirds of time is compute/branch, not memory. Achieved bandwidth peaks at 11.05 GB/s (37% of 29.9 GB/s ceiling) at q=0.01, falling to 4.81 GB/s (16%) at q=0.5. Compute-bound at low q (75–81% compute), branch-bound by q=0.5 (30–33% branch_flush). Against baseline: 0.83–0.91× at q=0.01, eroding to 0.99–1.04× at q=0.5. Against the winner: 1.35–1.75× slower at q=0.01, widening to 2.4–2.6× at q=0.5.

## Assembly
Loop 1 achieves partial vectorization: `fmul.4s` and `fadd.4s` on 4-wide float vectors for pos+vel, with `ext.16b` component rearrangement, but an indexed `ld1.s {v16}[1]` gather breaks the stream. Loop 2 is entirely scalar: 24 conditional branches, 18 `csel` for clamping, 19 `strb` byte-granular framebuffer stores, 21 scalar FP ops. The `fcmp`/`b.ge` death chain and `ldrb`/`csel`/`strb` blend pattern prevent vectorization. Only 9 of 297 instructions are vector-suffixed, all in loop 1.

## Verdict
Partially holds. Loop 1's vectorization (`fmul.4s`, `fadd.4s`) beats naive (0.83× baseline at q=0.01), but loop 2's byte-granular scatter and 24-branch respawn cap bandwidth at 37% of ceiling; branch_flush rises to 33% at q=0.5, erasing the advantage to parity (0.99–1.04× baseline). The winner is 1.35–2.6× faster at every point — register-resident verdicts cannot overcome the scatter's byte-store bottleneck.
